Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html

## Build and supply chain[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#build-and-supply-chain)

This page states WELD's build and supply chain practices, one per heading, each with the rule and the tag that shows whether the stack holds it today.

### W30: Support only PHP versions that are not end of life[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w30-support-only-php-versions-that-are-not-end-of-life)

**Practice:** `composer.json` requires `php: ^8.3` with `config.platform.php` `8.3.0`. Tests run on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. Laravel 13 needs 8.3 or newer.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `composer.json` requires `php: ^8.3`, `composer.json` sets `config.platform.php` to `8.3.0`, and the CI matrix runs on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 (`.gitlab-ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`).

### W31: Keep dev tools inside the PHP floor[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w31-keep-dev-tools-inside-the-php-floor)

**Practice:** Pest 5 requires PHP `^8.4`. On a `^8.3` floor use Pest 4 or PHPUnit and cap the constraint.

**Stack:** `Checked`. WELD runs Pest 4: `composer.json` requires `pestphp/pest ^4` (Pest 5 needs PHP `^8.4`), and the CI matrix starts at 8.3 (`.gitlab-ci.yml`), so `composer install` runs on 8.3 and would fail if a dev tool required 8.4 or newer. The PHPUnit class tests still run, under Pest.

### W32: Pinstripe owns style and static analysis[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w32-pinstripe-owns-style-and-static-analysis)

**Practice:** Use Pinstripe's Pint preset, PHPStan level 8 through Larastan, ESLint (flat config) and Prettier. No local overrides without a recorded reason.

**Stack:** `Checked`, for the PHP side. `composer.json` runs `pint --test`, `composer.json` runs `phpstan analyse`, and both are in the `ci` script (`composer.json`), which CI runs; `pint.json` uses the `laravel` preset and `phpstan.neon` sets `level: 8`. The JS side runs in CI too: the `frontend` job (`.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs `npm run lint` (`eslint.config.js`, flat config) and `npm run format:check` (`.prettierrc`). Pinstripe is not a dependency yet, so the presets are copied, not included.

### W33: Pin shared CI components to a commit[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w33-pin-shared-ci-components-to-a-commit)

**Practice:** Preflight components are referenced by commit SHA or a fixed tag, not a moving branch.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `.gitlab-ci.yml` pins every Preflight component to the 0.1.4 release SHA (the tag in a trailing comment) and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins the reusable workflow to a commit SHA; the comment "Pinned to Preflight 0.1.4. Never use ~latest." sits at the top of `.gitlab-ci.yml`. PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check, run by the `proctor-root` job, fails on an include without a SHA.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#related)

- [Security](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html)
- [Configuration](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

## Check your setup[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#check-your-setup)

Use `weld:doctor` to strike an arc across the local setup and see, one line per check, whether every joint holds.

### What it checks[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#what-it-checks)

`weld:doctor` strikes an arc across the local setup and reports every joint: the app key, writable storage, the database and pending migrations. One line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL. The checks, by name:

- `app-key`: PASS when `APP_KEY` is set; FAIL when it is empty, with a pointer to `php artisan key:generate`.
- `storage-writable`: PASS when `storage` and `bootstrap/cache` are both writable; FAIL when either is missing or not writable.
- `database`: PASS when the connection is up; FAIL names the exception class only, never the DSN, host or password.
- `migrations`: PASS when there are no pending migrations; WARN when some are pending (it lists them) or when it could not inspect them.

### Run it[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#run-it)

Run it through the OS scripts or straight to the container:

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
```

macOS / Linux

```sh
bin/weld.sh doctor
```

Container

```sh
docker compose run --rm app php artisan weld:doctor
```

### Read the report[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#read-the-report)

Each check prints one line: PASS, WARN or FAIL. The exit code is 1 when anything FAILs and 0 otherwise, so it works as a gate. Add `--json` to any of them for a machine-readable report. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.

Note

The standards checks (PHP version, debug in production, secure session cookies) belong to PROCTOR: run `composer proctor`, and the doctor report says so.

Not sure whether you want `weld:doctor`, `squire doctor` or `proctor check`? [Which command when](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/which-command.html) puts every look-alike side by side.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#related)

- [Which command when](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/which-command.html)
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html)
- [Oracle](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html

## The container contract[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#the-container-contract)

This page lists the container contract practices for WELD, from the BEST_PRACTICES guide, with the tag that says whether the stack holds each one today.

### W9. Config comes from the environment only[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w9-config-comes-from-the-environment-only)

**Practice:** No `.env` in the image. Call `env()` only inside `config/*.php`.

**Why:** After `config:cache` the `.env` file is not loaded and `env()` returns `null` elsewhere.

**Stack:** `Documented`. Every `env()` call in the app is inside `config/*.php`; none is in `app/` or `routes/`. The one exception is `bootstrap/app.php`, which reads `TRUSTED_PROXIES` with `env()` because that closure runs before config loads (it carries a PHPStan ignore). Target `Checked`: Pinstripe/PROCTOR ban `env(` outside `config/`; the portability job boots without `.env`.

### W10. `config:cache` runs at container start, never at image build[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w10-config-cache-runs-at-container-start-never-at-image-build)

**Practice:** Build time may run `route:cache`, `view:cache`, `event:cache`. `php artisan optimize` at start is acceptable if the build did not freeze config.

**Why:** A build-time `config:cache` freezes the build machine's environment into the image.

**Stack:** `Documented`. The image build runs no artisan commands: `deploy/build.sh` fails if app source is present at build time, and the release step runs `php artisan optimize` once the environment is in place (`deploy/scripts/release.sh`, on by default, off with `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_OPTIMIZE=0`), so config is cached at deploy, never at build. Target `Checked`: PROCTOR scans the Dockerfile.

### W11. `/up` is the liveness endpoint, and it never checks the database[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w11-up-is-the-liveness-endpoint-and-it-never-checks-the-database)

**Practice:** Keep Laravel's `/up` (200 when the app boots). It must answer for any `Host`, over plain HTTP, before trusted hosts, redirects, sessions, CSP and auth. Put database and cache checks on a separate `/ready` endpoint, through the `DiagnosingHealth` event or a package.

**Why:** A database blip must not make the orchestrator kill every web container.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `bootstrap/app.php` sets the health route to `/up`, which answers 200 when the framework boots and touches no database. The `/ready` endpoint is not built yet. Target `Checked`: the portability job requests `/up` with `Host: 10.1.2.3:8080` and no forwarded headers, and again with the database stopped.

### W12. Image health check matches the platform[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w12-image-health-check-matches-the-platform)

**Practice:** Put a `HEALTHCHECK` in the Dockerfile that calls `/up` with a tool the image has (`curl` or `wget`). On Coolify a Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` takes precedence over the dashboard check, and a dashboard check needs `curl` or `wget` inside the container.

**Why:** Traefik will not route to an unhealthy container, and a missing tool makes a healthy app look dead.

**Stack:** `Documented`. The Dockerfile carries a `HEALTHCHECK` (`deploy/.squire/Dockerfile`) whose script asks the local web server for `/up` by default and reads no database (`deploy/health.php`, `deploy/health.php`). Target `Checked`: Preflight portability runs `docker inspect` for a health status of `healthy`.

### W13. Non-root, arbitrary UID in group 0, listen on 8080[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w13-non-root-arbitrary-uid-in-group-0-listen-on-8080)

**Practice:** Declare a non-root `USER`. Make writable paths group 0 and group-writable (`chgrp -R 0`, `chmod -R g=u`) for `storage/` and `bootstrap/cache/`. Do not depend on a `www-data` entry. Honor `PORT`.

**Why:** OpenShift runs a random UID in group 0 with all capabilities dropped.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. A Dockerfile now exists (`deploy/.squire/Dockerfile`), but it is the Citadel Apache image: it declares no `USER`, the vhost listens on 80 (`deploy/.squire/vhost.conf`) and the fallback base exposes 80 (`deploy/.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile`), so the non-root, group-0, 8080 contract is not held. Target `Checked`: Preflight portability starts the image with a UID that has no `/etc/passwd` entry, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges` and a read-only root filesystem.

### W14. Logs go to stderr; the app writes only where it may[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w14-logs-go-to-stderr-the-app-writes-only-where-it-may)

**Practice:** Set `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr`. Nothing under `storage/logs`. Writes go to `storage/`, `bootstrap/cache/`, `/tmp` and declared volumes. Uploads go to object storage.

**Why:** Platforms collect stdout/stderr; local files vanish with the container.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `.env.example` sets `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr`. Target `Checked`: the portability job fails when `storage/logs` is non-empty.

### W15. Sessions and cache live in a shared store[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w15-sessions-and-cache-live-in-a-shared-store)

**Practice:** Use `SESSION_DRIVER=database` (or Redis) and a shared cache, even for one replica. Every host overlaps old and new containers during a deploy.

**Why:** A login must survive a hop between replicas.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `.env.example` sets `SESSION_DRIVER=database` and `.env.example` sets `CACHE_STORE=database`; `config/session.php` and `config/cache.php` default to the same. Target `Checked`: the portability job logs in on replica A and reads the session on replica B.

### W16. Stop cleanly on SIGTERM[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w16-stop-cleanly-on-sigterm)

**Practice:** Run PHP as PID 1 under a small init, or an entrypoint that `exec`s the server. Queue workers finish the current job on `SIGTERM`. Set the platform's grace period above the longest job `#[Timeout]`.

**Why:** A hard kill mid-job double-runs it after `retry_after`.

**Stack:** `Documented`. The entrypoint replaces the shell with the server (`deploy/.squire/fallback/citadel-apache-entrypoint`), so `SIGTERM` reaches the foreground process directly; no queue worker process type exists yet, and the grace period is a platform setting. Target `Checked`: the portability job sends `SIGTERM` and requires exit 0 within the grace period.

### W17. Trust proxies by preset, never `*` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w17-trust-proxies-by-preset-never)

**Practice:** Select a HELMET preset (`citadel` or `docker`), or list the front proxy in `HELMET_PROXIES` on other platforms. Do not paste `trustProxies(at: '*')` from tutorials. Set `APP_URL` and trusted hosts; Laravel trusts subdomains of `APP_URL` unless `subdomains: false`.

**Why:** An app that trusts all proxies lets a client forge `X-Forwarded-*` and the host used in callbacks.

**Stack:** `Enforced` by HELMET 0.3 (required `^0.3`): it trusts only the preset or listed proxies and drops `X-Forwarded-Port`. Target `Checked`: a portability probe sends forged `X-Forwarded-Host` and `-Proto` from an untrusted peer.

### How to read the tags[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#how-to-read-the-tags)

Each practice ends with exactly one tag.

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Enforced` | WELD's code does it or refuses to run without it, and a test covers it. |
| `Checked` | PROCTOR or CI warns or fails. |
| `Documented` | Written down in the README or a config file, with no check behind it. |
| `Not yet` | A gap. |

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#related)

- [App structure](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html)
- [Queues and scheduling](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

## Oracle[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#oracle)

Set up and check WELD's Oracle connection: the settings, the plain-language check, and the parity image for a real connection from your machine.

### The wiring[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#the-wiring)

WELD speaks Oracle through `yajra/laravel-oci8`, and the wiring is already in: an `oracle` connection in `config/database.php`, a check command, and plain-language sentences for the common errors. Until you set the Oracle settings it stays dormant: nothing connects and nothing errors.

### Set the settings[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#set-the-settings)

Fill in one set of names in `.env` (the commented block in `.env.example`): `ORACLE_USERNAME`, `ORACLE_PASSWORD`, and either `ORACLE_TNS` (an Easy Connect string, `host:port/service`, or a full descriptor) or `ORACLE_HOST`, `ORACLE_PORT` and `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME`. Leave them empty if your app does not use Oracle; nothing connects until they are set. On a server, set them in the app's environment settings, never in a file in git.

### Check the connection[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#check-the-connection)

Check the settings and the connection in plain language, one line per finding:

```
php artisan oracle:check
```

`oracle:check` is a thin wire to Squire's shared check file: it runs `deploy/oracle-check.php` with the current environment, streams the plain-language lines straight through, and returns the check's exit code, 0 when Oracle is not configured or all passed and 1 when a problem was found. The check file promises to never print a setting value. WELD does not own the check; a kit refresh (`vendor/bin/squire update`) puts the file here. If the check file is not there yet, the command tells you to run `vendor/bin/squire update` to get it.

### A real connection from your machine[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#a-real-connection-from-your-machine)

The local `app` container runs the stock Composer image, which has no Oracle driver. When you need a real connection from your machine, the Oracle-ready image is opt-in through `compose.oracle.yaml`:

PowerShell

```powershell
$env:WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE = "squire/oracle-parity:8.3"
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.oracle.yaml up
```

macOS / Linux

```sh
WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE=squire/oracle-parity:8.3 docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.oracle.yaml up
```

The overlay swaps only the app's image and passes the `ORACLE_*` settings through from `.env`; the ports stay bound to `127.0.0.1`. It fails closed when `WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE` is unset.

`squire/oracle-parity:8.3` is the name Squire documents for its parity image; build it once with Squire's `scripts/oracle-image-build.sh --flavour parity --php 8.3` (the name is a placeholder until a registry is chosen).

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#related)

- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html)
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html

## Queues and scheduling[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#queues-and-scheduling)

This page lists the queue and scheduling practices for WELD without Citadel workers, from the BEST_PRACTICES guide, with the tag that says whether the stack holds each one today.

### W18. Database queue by default; the worker is a process type[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w18-database-queue-by-default-the-worker-is-a-process-type)

**Practice:** `QUEUE_CONNECTION=database`; run `php artisan queue:work --max-time=3600 --tries=3` as the `worker` process where the platform allows one. Use `#[Tries]`, `#[Timeout]` and `#[Backoff]` on jobs.

**Why:** It needs no extra service, and `--max-time` recycles memory.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `.env.example` sets `QUEUE_CONNECTION=database`, `config/queue.php` defaults to it, and the jobs tables are migrated by `database/migrations/0001_01_01_000002_create_jobs_table.php`. No job classes exist yet, so the `#[Tries]`/`#[Timeout]`/`#[Backoff]` attributes are not in use. Target `Checked`: a test that every job class declares `#[Tries]` and `#[Timeout]`.

### W19. Where no worker can run, run the queue from the scheduler[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w19-where-no-worker-can-run-run-the-queue-from-the-scheduler)

**Practice:** On Citadel (no queue workers), schedule `queue:work --stop-when-empty --max-time=50 --tries=3` every minute with `withoutOverlapping` and a short expiry. Select it with `WELD_QUEUE_MODE=scheduled`.

**Why:** `--stop-when-empty` is documented for Docker use ("shutdown the container after the queue is empty"), and the scheduler is the one cron entry Citadel can run. This exact pattern is an inference, not a documented recipe.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. `routes/console.php` has no scheduler entries yet (only the `inspire` command). Target `Checked`: a test that `schedule:list` shows the entry under the `citadel` preset and not under the others.

### W20. Timeout below `retry_after` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w20-timeout-below-retry-after)

**Practice:** Set each job timeout lower than the connection's `retry_after`. Timeouts need the PCNTL extension.

**Why:** Otherwise the job is attempted again before it has finished.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. No job classes exist yet. Target `Checked`: a config test comparing the two values; the image installs `pcntl`.

### W21. One scheduler entry; one run per task[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w21-one-scheduler-entry-one-run-per-task)

**Practice:** Run `php artisan schedule:run` every minute (cron, or a CronJob), or `schedule:work` for a single long-lived container. With more than one scheduler, mark tasks `onOneServer()` (shared cache) and name closures.

**Why:** Three schedulers run a nightly report three times.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. `routes/console.php` has no scheduler entries yet. Target `Checked`: a test fails on any scheduled closure without `->name()`.

### W22. Interrupt and restart long-lived processes at deploy[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w22-interrupt-and-restart-long-lived-processes-at-deploy)

**Practice:** After a release run `php artisan queue:restart` (or `php artisan reload`), and `schedule:interrupt` when sub-minute tasks exist.

**Why:** Workers and a minute-long `schedule:run` keep the old code until they exit.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. The release script now exists (`deploy/scripts/release.sh`) but runs none of `queue:restart`, `reload` or `schedule:interrupt`. Target `Checked`: the release script lists the three commands; PROCTOR checks the file.

### W23. Make a silent scheduler visible[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w23-make-a-silent-scheduler-visible)

**Practice:** Record a heartbeat on every scheduler minute and fail `/ready` (not `/up`) when it is older than a few minutes. Export the age as a Prometheus gauge (off by default).

**Why:** With no worker supervisor, a stopped scheduler is otherwise invisible.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. There is no scheduler and no `/ready` endpoint yet. Target `Checked`: a test advances a fake clock and asserts `/ready` fails.

### W24. Run migrations exactly once per release[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w24-run-migrations-exactly-once-per-release)

**Practice:** Use a Job, a pre-deploy hook (Coolify "Pre-deployment Command"), or `migrate --isolated`. Never run `migrate` in a per-replica entrypoint.

**Why:** Parallel replicas race on schema changes.

**Stack:** `Documented`. The release step runs `php artisan migrate --force` (`deploy/scripts/release.sh`) once per release, from the first-release hook (`deploy/deployments/001-first-release.sh`) and the Quick Update post-script (`deploy/scripts/release.sh`); the entrypoint itself runs no artisan commands (`deploy/.squire/fallback/citadel-apache-entrypoint`). Target `Checked`: PROCTOR flags `migrate` in an entrypoint.

### How to read the tags[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#how-to-read-the-tags)

Each practice ends with exactly one tag.

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Enforced` | WELD's code does it or refuses to run without it, and a test covers it. |
| `Checked` | PROCTOR or CI warns or fails. |
| `Documented` | Written down in the README or a config file, with no check behind it. |
| `Not yet` | A gap. |

- [App structure](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html)
- [The container contract](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html)

## Quick start[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

This page takes a fresh copy of WELD from a folder to a running, checked app on your machine.

One command strikes the spark; the containers do the welding. Docker is the only prerequisite: PHP and Node run in the containers, so the host needs neither.

### Steps[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#steps)

1. Bring the stack up:
   PowerShell
   ```powershell
   .\bin\weld.ps1 up
   ```
   macOS / Linux
   ```sh
   bin/weld.sh up
   ```
   Expected: `up` copies `.env.example` to `.env` if it is missing, installs the PHP and Node dependencies in the containers, starts the app and Vite, generates the app key if it is not set, and runs the migrations.
2. Open [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000). Expected: the app, served by the local stack.
3. Run the doctor:
   PowerShell
   ```powershell
   .\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
   ```
   macOS / Linux
   ```sh
   bin/weld.sh doctor
   ```
   Expected: one line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL; exit code 1 when anything FAILs. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.
4. Run the checks:
   PowerShell
   ```powershell
   .\bin\weld.ps1 test
   ```
   macOS / Linux
   ```sh
   bin/weld.sh test
   ```
   Expected: `composer ci` runs in the app container: validate, tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready check and audit.

### The subcommands[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#the-subcommands)

The same subcommands work on every OS:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `up` | Bring the whole stack up, as above |
| `down` | Stop and remove the containers |
| `test` | Run `composer ci` in the app container |
| `doctor` | Run `php artisan weld:doctor` in the app container |
| `logs` | Follow the container logs |

### What you built[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-you-built)

You have WELD running locally in Docker: the app and Vite in containers, `.env` copied from `.env.example`, the app key generated and the migrations run. That is the whole Wayne State app stack joined into one application, with sign-in, security headers, checks, coding standards, CI and the WayneUI interface already hooked up. Open the app and every page you see (the welcome page, the dashboard, settings) is drawn by WayneUI's components, light or dark to match your device.

### Next steps[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps)

- Make it yours: rename the four things that still say WELD (the composer name, the app name, the site title and the git remote), give the copy its own key, and re-run the checks.
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html): what the doctor reports, joint by joint.
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html): the parts and what each does in the app.
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html): for when the destination is somewhere other than a laptop.

## Is WELD still Sourdough's shape?[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html#is-weld-still-sourdough-s-shape)

This page shows how the regen gate proves that WELD is still Sourdough's Inertia shape, and how to run it against your own generation.

### How the check works[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html#how-the-check-works)

Sourdough writes a manifest of every file it generates (`.sourdough/manifest.json`: each path with its SHA-256). `bin/regen-check.php` compares that manifest with WELD file by file, skipping the product files WELD adds on top (listed in `.sourdough/product-files.json`) and any path with a `vendor` or `node_modules` segment. Each remaining path is reported as IDENTICAL, DIFFERS or MISSING_IN_WELD.

The generated app folder must contain `.sourdough/manifest.json`, the file list Sourdough writes into every app it generates (files maps path to `{class, sha256}`). Paths listed in `.sourdough/product-files.json` (exact paths or `dir/` prefixes) and every path with a `vendor` or `node_modules` segment at any depth are skipped. A DIFFERS path means the WELD file exists with another SHA-256.

### The ratchet baseline[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html#the-ratchet-baseline)

The gate is a ratchet: `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` records the drift already known and accepted, and the check fails only on new drift. CI runs it against a fresh `sourdough new --inertia` generation from Sourdough's main, and the GitLab `regen-gate` job blocks on new drift; locally, point it at your own generation. When it reports new drift, fix it here or upstream in Sourdough; if the drift is accepted as intended, record the current drift as accepted with `--write-baseline` and commit `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json`.

### Running the check[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html#running-the-check)

Run the check:

```sh
php bin/regen-check.php --generated <dir>
```

or through Composer:

```sh
composer regen-check -- --generated <dir>
```

Record the current drift as accepted: add `--write-baseline`.

Note

Exit codes: 0 no new drift (or the baseline was written), 1 new drift, listed on stderr, 2 usage error. The script is plain PHP 8.3 with no Composer packages, so it runs on Windows, macOS and Linux the same way.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html#related)

- [WELD and Sourdough](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html)
- [Status](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/status.html)
- [Changelog](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html)

## Security[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#security)

This page states WELD's security practices, one per heading, each with the rule and the tag that shows whether the stack holds it today.

### W25: Keep the framework above the published security floor[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#w25-keep-the-framework-above-the-published-security-floor)

**Practice:** Require `laravel/framework` at or above the latest patched release, run `composer audit` in CI, and let CREED's `policy.json` name the minimum patch level. A critical TokenGuard authentication bypass was published on 2026-10-19 (fixed in 13.29.0 and 12.68.0).

**Stack:** `Checked`. `composer.json` pins `laravel/framework: ^13.29` (at or above the patched release), `composer.json` runs `@composer audit` inside the `ci` script, and `.gitlab-ci.yml` includes the Preflight `composer-audit` component, so the audit runs in CI. CREED's `policy.json` is a dependency and PROCTOR measures against it, now also inside the test suite (`tests/Feature/ProctorCheckTest.php`).

### W26: Debug is off outside local[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#w26-debug-is-off-outside-local)

Warning

`APP_DEBUG=false` in production. Debug pages expose configuration values, and the debug page has had an XSS advisory (Low, 2026-09-10).

**Practice:** `APP_DEBUG=false` in production. The debug page has had an XSS advisory (Low, 2026-09-10).

**Stack:** `Not yet`. `.env.example` sets `APP_DEBUG=true` for the local default, and there is no boot assertion that fails when `APP_ENV=production` and `APP_DEBUG=true`. Target `Enforced`: a boot assertion fails when `APP_ENV=production` and `APP_DEBUG=true`.

### W27: CSRF uses the PreventRequestForgery middleware[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#w27-csrf-uses-the-preventrequestforgery-middleware)

**Practice:** Laravel 13 formalized request-forgery protection as `PreventRequestForgery` (origin-aware, still token-compatible). Any custom middleware stack or HELMET code must reference the new name.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `bootstrap/app.php` appends to the default `web` middleware group, which carries `PreventRequestForgery` in Laravel 13, so the protection is in place by default. There is no feature test that posts without a token and expects 419. Target `Checked`: a feature test posts without a token and expects 419.

### W28: CSP works with Inertia 3 and Vite[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#w28-csp-works-with-inertia-3-and-vite)

**Practice:** HELMET sets the CSP header and calls `Vite::useCspNonce()`; Laravel then adds the nonce to the tags `@vite` emits. Inertia 3 puts initial page data in a JSON script element. Run the policy in report-only first.

**Stack:** `Documented`. HELMET `^0.3` is a dependency and its security headers and CSP middleware run in the global chain. Target `Checked`: a browser test under an enforced CSP.

### W29: Agent tooling stays out of production[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#w29-agent-tooling-stays-out-of-production)

Warning

A dev tool with write and query abilities is attack surface. Its MCP server can write rules to disk and run database queries, and its docs tool sends queries to a hosted service. Keep it out of production: build production images with `composer install --no-dev`.

**Practice:** Laravel Boost is `require-dev`. Its MCP server can write rules to disk and run database queries; its docs tool sends queries to a hosted service. Production images are built with `composer install --no-dev`; guard any `post-update-cmd` that calls `boost:update`.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. Boost is not a dependency yet. Target `Checked`: the portability job fails when `vendor/laravel/boost` exists in the image.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#related)

- [Build and supply chain](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html)
- [Configuration](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

## WELD and Sourdough[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html#weld-and-sourdough)

This page explains how Sourdough and WELD divide the work of starting a Wayne State app, and which one to pick for your project.

### What Sourdough does[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html#what-sourdough-does)

Sourdough is the starter tool for every shape of Wayne State app. It bakes all five: raw PHP, raw PHP with a Vue SPA, Laravel with Blade, Laravel with Blade plus Vue islands, and Laravel with Inertia and Vue.

### Where WELD sits[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html#where-weld-sits)

WELD is one of those shapes, Laravel with Inertia and Vue, with every part already joined and proved to work together. In other words, WELD is the Laravel + Inertia/Vue shape that Sourdough's templates describe, already shaped.

Note

Pick Sourdough when you want a starter you shape yourself. Pick WELD when you want the finished piece.

### Where changes belong[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html#where-changes-belong)

If every app should get a change, it belongs in Sourdough; if only this shape should, it lives here.

## What is welded in[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html#what-is-welded-in)

This page lists the parts welded into WELD, what each one does in the app, and what is on the bench today.

### The parts[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html#the-parts)

| Part | What it does in WELD |
| --- | --- |
| WayneUI | The interface: Wayne State's design system, 2.0.8 from npm, pinned exactly. Its app bar, sidebar drawer, cards, forms and dialog draw every page, in light and dark, and ESLint keeps any other component kit out |
| CREED | The written standards and `policy.json`: supported PHP, Laravel and Node versions |
| Pinstripe | The coding standard: Pint, PHPStan level 8, ESLint and Prettier |
| Preflight | The CI pipeline, from GitLab CI/CD components |
| PROCTOR | The checks, run in CI and as the deploy gate |
| SESAME | Sign-in: CAS, Entra ID (OpenID Connect) and the auth gateway driver, and app-native sessions |
| HELMET | The baseline runtime: security headers and CSP, sessions, trusted proxies, `/up` |
| Ziggy | Route names as URLs: the route list ships inside the Vite bundle, so `route()` works in Vue templates and scripts without an inline script |

![WELD's journey, one request and six stops joined by a gold seam: HELMET sets security headers, SESAME signs the user in, WayneUI renders the page, PROCTOR checks the code, Preflight runs CI, Squire deploys.](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/journey.svg)

One request, six stops, one seam. The bead runs the length of it; with reduced motion on, it stays put.

### What is on the bench today[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html#what-is-on-the-bench-today)

HELMET, SESAME and PROCTOR are welded in from Packagist; the rest of the cast is on Packagist too and gets welded on in turn.

- `composer.json` is `waynestate/weld`, requires PHP `^8.3`, and the lock file resolves for 8.3.0
- `.env.example` sets `APP_NAME=WELD`, `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr` and `SESSION_DRIVER=database`
- `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` keeps index keys under Citadel's MySQL 5.6 767-byte cap
- `.gitattributes` sets `* text=auto eol=lf`
- `composer ci` is the CI contract: it runs validate, tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready check and audit, the same command on GitLab and GitHub
- `pint.json` and `phpstan.neon` still copy Pinstripe's 0.1 Laravel presets; Pinstripe 0.1.4 is on Packagist (tagged), and they switch to `includes: vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/...` when WELD requires it
- HELMET runs its security headers and CSP middleware in the global chain, so every response carries the baseline; the Vite build takes the per-request nonce; trusted proxies are a literal list in `bootstrap/app.php`; `/up` stays Laravel's built-in health route
- SESAME owns sign-in at `/login` and `/logout`; the fake driver stands in for the identity provider locally, and CAS is an env change away
- PROCTOR measures WELD against CREED's `policy.json` as a CI job (`composer proctor`): warnings pass, failures block
- The starter kit's password auth (register, login, password reset, two-factor) is removed on purpose; the door is SESAME's
- WayneUI draws the Vue pages: `resources/css/app.css` imports its layered stylesheet, the pages use `@waynestate/wayne-ui-vue` components, and the appearance setting is WayneUI's own theme switch (`wsu-theme`), with the bar's sun and moon button in step. The starter kit's Tailwind theme and shadcn-vue copies are gone, and `npm run lint` fails on an import from a `components/ui` folder
- The license is MIT

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html#related)

- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html)
- [Oracle](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html)

## Overview[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#overview)

This page orients you to WELD: what it is, which path to pick first, and where the project stands today.

[![WELD's front page: the headline WELD, 'Wired, Everything, Linked, Deployed. Many parts, one piece.', the composer create-project command, and the welder's-helmet mark on a green tile.](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/hero.jpg)](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/index.html)

**WELD**

![php ^8.3](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/php.svg) ![laravel ^13.29](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/laravel.svg) ![license MIT](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/license.svg)

**W**ired, **E**verything, **L**inked, **D**eployed. Many parts, one piece.

WELD is the whole Wayne State app stack joined into one application. Install it, deploy it, and every part is already hooked up: sign-in, security headers, checks, coding standards, CI and the WayneUI interface. Think of it as the Megazord, except it comes with a deploy script and nobody has to shout to make it combine. Fourteen parts, one bead.

### Pick your path[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): bring the whole stack up with one Docker command.
- [Install](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): get a copy with composer create-project, or clone it if you want the history too.
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html): the parts and what each does in the app.
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html): OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker, with Citadel for comparison.

### Status[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#status)

Latest release: 0.1.5 (2026-11-07). The license is MIT.

**Not to be confused with:** `weld:doctor` checks local setup only; standards checks are PROCTOR's.

Agents: fetch [https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt).

## Install[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

This page gets you a working copy of WELD: what it needs, the two ways to get it, and how to verify the result.

### Requirements[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

- PHP `^8.3`
- Laravel `^13.29`
- Node, for `npm ci`
- Docker, for the local stack

Note

To run WELD locally, Docker is the only prerequisite: PHP and Node run in the containers, so the host needs neither.

### Get it[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#get-it)

WELD is an app you start from, not a library you require. The Megazord ships in a repo, not a box. Composer makes you a fresh copy, writes `.env`, generates the app key and runs the first migration:

```sh
composer create-project waynestate/weld my-app
cd my-app
npm ci
```

Note

`create-project` installs the newest tagged release, and `main` can be ahead of it: the [Changelog](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html) lists what is unreleased. 0.1.3 (2026-11-06) is the first tag where WayneUI draws the app; 0.1.2 was from before it (see [Proof](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html)). Clone when you want `main`.

Or clone it, if you want the history too, and it is yours to rename:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/weld.git my-app
cd my-app
composer install
php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
npm ci
# Windows (PowerShell):
Copy-Item .env.example .env
# Linux/macOS:
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
```

Note

The `advisor install` line writes `.mcp.json`, the MCP config that points Claude Code at ADVISOR's server; the file is git-ignored, because a committed `.mcp.json` would run a program on whoever opens the project. Set `ADVISOR_ENABLED=1` in `.env` to switch the advisor on.

### Verify[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

Run the checks the way CI does. `composer ci` is the CI contract: it runs validate, tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready check and audit, the same command on GitLab and GitHub. The `test` subcommand runs it in the app container: `.\bin\weld.ps1 test` on Windows (PowerShell), `bin/weld.sh test` on macOS / Linux.

The doctor strikes an arc across the local setup: `.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor` on Windows (PowerShell), `bin/weld.sh doctor` on macOS / Linux. It reports one line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL, and exits with code 1 when anything FAILs, so it works as a gate. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.

### Next steps[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#next-steps)

- [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): bring the stack up with one command and open the app.
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html): the parts already hooked up in your copy.
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html): what the doctor reports, joint by joint.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#related)

- [Overview](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/index.html)
- [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html)

## Commands[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands)

This page is the reference for every command a WELD app runs: the `bin/weld` subcommands, the composer scripts, and the artisan and bin PHP commands, with what each one does.

### The bin/weld subcommands[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#the-bin-weld-subcommands)

One command strikes the spark; the containers do the welding. Docker is the only prerequisite: PHP and Node run in the containers, so the host needs neither. The same subcommands work on every OS.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `up` | Copy `.env.example` to `.env` if missing, install the PHP and Node dependencies in the containers, write `.mcp.json` from ADVISOR, start the app and Vite, generate the app key if needed, and migrate |
| `down` | Stop and remove the containers |
| `test` | Run `composer ci` in the app container |
| `doctor` | Run `php artisan weld:doctor` in the app container |
| `logs` | Follow the container logs; Ctrl+C stops |

Tip

`up` finishes with a pointer to open [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000). Skip the ADVISOR step with `--no-advisor` (`-NoAdvisor` on Windows).

Bring the whole stack up:

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 up
```

sh

```sh
bin/weld.sh up
```

Run the full check suite in the app container:

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 test
```

sh

```sh
bin/weld.sh test
```

Check your setup:

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
```

sh

```sh
bin/weld.sh doctor
```

Follow the container logs:

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 logs
```

sh

```sh
bin/weld.sh logs
```

Stop and remove the containers:

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 down
```

sh

```sh
bin/weld.sh down
```

### Composer scripts[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#composer-scripts)

| Script | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `composer test` | Pest, running the PHPUnit class tests and the Pest tests side by side |
| `composer lint` | Run Pint as a check (`pint --test`) |
| `composer fix` | Apply Pint fixes (`pint`) |
| `composer analyse` | Run PHPStan analysis (`phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G`) |
| `composer proctor` | PROCTOR against CREED's policy |
| `composer ziggy` | Confirm the Ziggy routes are current: `composer ziggy`, then `git diff --exit-code resources/js/ziggy.*` |
| `composer regen-check` | Compare a freshly generated Sourdough Inertia app with WELD by SHA-256 and fail only on new drift versus `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json`; pass `--generated <dir>` (and optionally `--write-baseline`) through |
| `composer ci` | Runs `composer validate --strict`, the tests, Pint, PHPStan, the agent-ready and docs checks and `composer audit`; it does not run PROCTOR, Ziggy or the JS lint |
| `composer site:agent-ready` | Rewrite the Markdown twins, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, robots.txt and sitemap.xml in site/ (Squire's agent-ready kit) |
| `composer site:agent-ready-check` | Fail when the agent-ready files are stale, a page lacks its Markdown link, a prompt drifts from the docs, or the kit was edited here |
| `composer docs` | Write site/docs/ from docs/ with the shared docs builder, and generate docs/changelog.md from CHANGELOG.md |
| `composer docs:check` | Fail when the committed docs site is stale or the docs carry findings; writes nothing |

### Artisan and bin PHP commands[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#artisan-and-bin-php-commands)

#### `php artisan weld:doctor` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#php-artisan-weld-doctor)

`weld:doctor` strikes an arc across the local setup and reports every joint: the app key, writable storage, the database and pending migrations. One line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL; exit code 1 when anything FAILs, so it works as a gate. The standards checks (PHP version, debug in production, secure session cookies) belong to PROCTOR: run `composer proctor`, and the doctor report says so. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.

Add `--json` to any of these for a machine-readable report. Run it through the `doctor` subcommand above, or straight to the container:

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
```

sh

```sh
bin/weld.sh doctor
```

Docker

```sh
docker compose run --rm app php artisan weld:doctor
```

#### `php bin/regen-check.php` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#php-bin-regen-check-php)

`bin/regen-check.php` compares a freshly generated Sourdough Inertia app (its `.sourdough/manifest.json`, each path with its SHA-256) with WELD file by file, skipping the product files listed in `.sourdough/product-files.json` and any `vendor` or `node_modules` path. Each remaining path is reported as IDENTICAL, DIFFERS, MISSING_IN_WELD or RELOCATED. The gate is a ratchet: `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` records the drift already known and accepted, and the check fails only on new drift. It is not part of `composer ci`; CI runs it as a separate job that blocks on new drift.

- Run the check: `php bin/regen-check.php --generated <dir>` (or `composer regen-check -- --generated <dir>`)
- Record the current drift as accepted: add `--write-baseline`

#### `php bin/agent-ready.php` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#php-bin-agent-ready-php)

- `php bin/agent-ready.php`: rewrite the Markdown twins, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, robots.txt and sitemap.xml in site/ (Squire's agent-ready kit).
- `php bin/agent-ready.php --check`: fail when the agent-ready files are stale, a page lacks its Markdown link, a prompt drifts from the docs, or the kit was edited here.

These run as `composer site:agent-ready` and `composer site:agent-ready-check`.

#### `php bin/docs-site.php` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#php-bin-docs-site-php)

- `php bin/docs-site.php`: write site/docs/ from docs/ with the shared docs builder, and generate docs/changelog.md from CHANGELOG.md.
- `php bin/docs-site.php --check`: fail when the committed docs site is stale or the docs carry findings; writes nothing.

These run as `composer docs` and `composer docs:check`. The docs are built from `docs/` by the shared docs builder and checked in `composer ci`, so the page you read is the page that ships.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#related)

- [Which command when](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/which-command.html): `weld:doctor`, `squire doctor`, `proctor check` and the other look-alikes side by side
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html)

## Configuration[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#configuration)

This page lists every environment variable a WELD app reads, its default from `.env.example`, and what the sources say about it.

### Environment variables[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#environment-variables)

| Name | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_NAME` | `WELD` | Renamed when you clone and rename; `VITE_APP_NAME` follows it through `${APP_NAME}`. |
| `APP_ENV` | `local` |  |
| `APP_KEY` | `(empty)` | Generate it with `php artisan key:generate`; `weld:doctor` checks the app key. |
| `APP_DEBUG` | `true` | The local default; keep `APP_DEBUG=false` in production (W26). |
| `APP_URL` | `http://localhost` | Set it to the real host (W17); Laravel trusts subdomains of `APP_URL` unless `subdomains: false`. |
| `APP_LOCALE` | `en` |  |
| `APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE` | `en` |  |
| `APP_FAKER_LOCALE` | `en_US` |  |
| `APP_MAINTENANCE_DRIVER` | `file` |  |
| `APP_MAINTENANCE_STORE` | `database (commented out)` |  |
| `PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS` | `4` |  |
| `BCRYPT_ROUNDS` | `12` |  |
| `LOG_CHANNEL` | `stderr` | Everything goes to `php://stderr`; nothing under `storage/logs` (W14). |
| `LOG_STACK` | `single` |  |
| `LOG_DEPRECATIONS_CHANNEL` | `null` |  |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `debug` |  |
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `sqlite` | Local development uses SQLite. |
| `DB_HOST` | `127.0.0.1 (commented out)` |  |
| `DB_PORT` | `3306 (commented out)` |  |
| `DB_DATABASE` | `laravel (commented out)` |  |
| `DB_USERNAME` | `root (commented out)` |  |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | `(empty, commented out)` |  |
| `ORACLE_USERNAME` | `(empty, commented out)` | Leave empty if the app does not use Oracle; nothing connects until set. On a server, set it in the app's environment settings, never in a file in git. |
| `ORACLE_PASSWORD` | `(empty, commented out)` | As `ORACLE_USERNAME`; on a server, set it in the app's environment settings, never in a file in git. |
| `ORACLE_TNS` | `(empty, commented out)` | An Easy Connect string (`host:port/service`) or a full descriptor; set this or the host, port and service trio. |
| `ORACLE_HOST` | `(empty, commented out)` | Set with `ORACLE_PORT` and `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME` as the alternative to `ORACLE_TNS`. |
| `ORACLE_PORT` | `(empty, commented out)` | Part of the host, port and service alternative to `ORACLE_TNS`. |
| `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME` | `(empty, commented out)` | Part of the host, port and service alternative to `ORACLE_TNS`. |
| `SESSION_DRIVER` | `database` | A shared store, even for one replica (W15). |
| `SESSION_LIFETIME` | `120` |  |
| `SESSION_ENCRYPT` | `false` |  |
| `SESSION_PATH` | `/` |  |
| `SESSION_DOMAIN` | `null` |  |
| `TRUSTED_PROXIES` | `172.18.0.1` | Which proxies Laravel trusts for `X-Forwarded-Proto` and the client address. Unset keeps `172.18.0.1` (Citadel's proxy); set but empty trusts none; `*` trusts every proxy; or a comma-separated list of IPs and CIDR ranges. Off Citadel, set your own proxy here and put the same list in `HELMET_PROXIES`. |
| `HELMET_PROXIES` | `172.18.0.1` | The address HA-Proxy connects from; the same list as `trustProxies` in `bootstrap/app.php`. Empty trusts nothing. A platform preset fills the list instead; when both are set, `HELMET_PROXIES` wins, and an unknown preset name throws at boot. |
| `HELMET_PRESET` | `citadel (commented out)` | Picks a platform preset; HELMET ships two, `citadel` and `docker`. An unknown preset name throws at boot. When both it and `HELMET_PROXIES` are set, `HELMET_PROXIES` wins. |
| `SESAME_DRIVER` | `fake` | SESAME owns sign-in. `fake` signs in locally without an identity provider and refuses to boot outside development environments; production sets `SESAME_DRIVER=cas` plus `SESAME_CAS_BASE_URL`. |
| `SESAME_FAKE_USERNAME` | `jdoe` |  |
| `SESAME_CAS_BASE_URL` | `(empty, commented out)` | Set with `SESAME_DRIVER=cas` in production. |
| `SESAME_CAS_SERVICE_URL` | `(empty, commented out)` |  |
| `BROADCAST_CONNECTION` | `log` |  |
| `FILESYSTEM_DISK` | `local` |  |
| `QUEUE_CONNECTION` | `database` | Run the queue worker where the platform allows one (W18). |
| `CACHE_STORE` | `database` | A shared cache, even for one replica (W15). |
| `CACHE_PREFIX` | `(empty, commented out)` |  |
| `MEMCACHED_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` |  |
| `REDIS_CLIENT` | `phpredis` |  |
| `REDIS_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` |  |
| `REDIS_PASSWORD` | `null` |  |
| `REDIS_PORT` | `6379` |  |
| `MAIL_MAILER` | `log` |  |
| `MAIL_SCHEME` | `null` |  |
| `MAIL_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` |  |
| `MAIL_PORT` | `2525` |  |
| `MAIL_USERNAME` | `null` |  |
| `MAIL_PASSWORD` | `null` |  |
| `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS` | `hello@example.com` |  |
| `MAIL_FROM_NAME` | `${APP_NAME}` |  |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | `(empty)` |  |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | `(empty)` |  |
| `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` | `us-east-1` |  |
| `AWS_BUCKET` | `(empty)` |  |
| `AWS_USE_PATH_STYLE_ENDPOINT` | `false` |  |
| `VITE_APP_NAME` | `${APP_NAME}` | Follows `APP_NAME` through `${APP_NAME}`. |

### Trusted proxies and HELMET_PRESET[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#trusted-proxies-and-helmet-preset)

HELMET owns the trusted proxies (W17, `Enforced` by HELMET 0.2): it trusts only the preset or listed proxies and drops `X-Forwarded-Port`. Pick a platform preset with `HELMET_PRESET`; HELMET 0.2 ships two, `citadel` and `docker`, and an unknown preset name throws at boot. On other platforms, list the front proxy's address in `HELMET_PROXIES` (it wins over `HELMET_PRESET`), and never trust a whole private range. Do not paste `trustProxies(at: '*')` from tutorials: an app that trusts all proxies lets a client forge `X-Forwarded-*` and the host used in callbacks. Laravel's own proxy list has its own variable; set `TRUSTED_PROXIES` to the same address (unset means Citadel's `172.18.0.1`). In WELD today, trusted proxies are a literal list in `bootstrap/app.php`.

### Keep .env out of version control[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#keep-env-out-of-version-control)

Warning

`.env` never goes into version control. On a server, set values in the app's environment settings, never in a file in git.

## Proof[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof)

This page says how WELD was proven on 2026-11-06: a new app made from a clean folder the way this site tells you to, every gate WELD ships run against it, and one small Wayne State app ported onto it. It lists what held, what broke, what was fixed that night, and what it does not prove yet. Next, see the [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html) for the steps the run followed and [Troubleshooting](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html) for the fixes it produced.

Welders prove a joint with a bend test: cut a strip across the seam, bend it double, and look for cracks. WELD's promise is that a Wayne State developer gets a full, working, accessible app quickly with the whole stack already joined. So the strip was a brand-new app, and the bending was done by a stopwatch, the app's own gates and a browser.

### Last run[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#last-run)

Run on one Windows machine with Docker Desktop; durations are wall clock, including dependency installs where a command makes them.

| Check | Date | Commit | Result | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composer ci` (Pest, Pint, PHPStan level 8, agent-ready, docs site, audit) | 2026-11-07 | `e555f03` | Pass: 90 tests (261 assertions), none risky; 67 files formatted; no PHPStan errors; no advisories | 163 s (warm vendor) |
| `composer proctor` | 2026-11-07 | `baf8e60` | Pass, 1 warning: the PHP 8.3 floor is in security-only support until 2027-12-31 | 176 s |
| `ziggy` job | 2026-11-07 | `baf8e60` | Pass: the regenerated route list matches the committed one | 174 s |
| `frontend` job (ESLint, Prettier, vue-tsc, Vite) | 2026-11-07 | `baf8e60` | Pass: lint, format and types clean; 168 modules built | 27 s |
| Accessibility gate (axe-core, WCAG 2.2 AA) | 2026-11-07 | `e555f03` | Pass: 23 pages, 0 violations, light and dark at 360 px and 1280 px | 70 s |
| Regen gate (a fresh `sourdough new --inertia` compared with WELD) | 2026-11-07 | `e555f03` | Pass: no new drift against Sourdough main `323a82b`; every differing or missing path is in the baseline | 60 s |
| `weld:doctor` | 2026-11-07 | `baf8e60` | Pass: 4 PASS (app key, storage, database, migrations) | 21 s |

Refresh it by re-running those seven checks at the current HEAD, writing down the new date and commit, and rebuilding the site with `composer docs` and `composer site:agent-ready`. The `composer ci`, accessibility and regen rows above are from this refresh at `e555f03`: the regen gate now passes against Sourdough's current main (`323a82b`), with no new drift beyond the recorded baseline, and the accessibility gate runs as `scripts/a11y.ps1` is written on Docker Desktop, checking all 23 committed pages with 0 violations. The `create-project` path, the signed-in app-page accessibility checks and the `up` timings are not in the table: the first installs the newest public tag instead of this commit, and the rest need the running stack and a browser.

### What ran[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-ran)

One Windows 11 machine with Docker Desktop, Node 24 and no PHP or Composer on the host, which is the setup the [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html) says is enough. Each path started from an empty folder. Every step was timed and logged, and nothing was retried to make a number look better.

1. **The `create-project` path** from [Install](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): `composer create-project waynestate/weld` (run in the `composer:2.10.3` image, since the host has no Composer), `npm ci`, then `bin\weld.ps1 up` and `test`.
2. **The clone path** from the [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): `git clone` from the GitHub mirror at `main` (`6da94b9`), `bin\weld.ps1 up`, then the pages in a browser and every gate WELD ships, run locally the way its CI runs them:
   - `bin\weld.ps1 doctor` and `bin\weld.ps1 test` (`composer ci`: validate, Pest, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready and docs checks, audit);
   - `composer proctor` against CREED's policy, the `proctor-root` CI job;
   - the `frontend` CI job: ESLint, Prettier, vue-tsc and the Vite build;
   - the `ziggy` CI job: regenerate the route list and fail on any diff;
   - the regen gate: a fresh `sourdough new --inertia` compared with WELD file by file;
   - an accessibility gate: axe-core with the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA rules on the welcome page, the dashboard and both settings pages, signed in through SESAME's fake driver, at desktop and phone width, light and dark, with reduced motion on (16 page checks).
3. **A port** onto the fresh clone: one small app from the stack's proof corpus, below.

### Results[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#results)

The clone path, the one the Quick start teaches:

| Step | Time | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `git clone` | 2 s | `main` at `6da94b9` |
| `bin\weld.ps1 up`, first time | 238 s | Up: Composer and npm installs, the app and Vite started, key generated, migrations run |
| Open `http://localhost:8000` |  | **Blank page.** Only HELMET's `local` ribbon drew. Fixed the same night, below |
| The pages, after the fix | 10 to 20 s for the first load, then instant | Welcome, dashboard, profile and appearance all drawn by WayneUI; SESAME's fake driver signed in as the fake user |
| `bin\weld.ps1 doctor` | 6 s | 4 PASS: app key, storage, database, migrations |
| `bin\weld.ps1 test` (`composer ci`) | 153 s | Pass: 85 tests (2 marked risky), Pint, PHPStan level 8, docs and agent-ready current, no advisories |
| `composer proctor` | 6 s | Pass, 1 warning (the PHP 8.3 floor is in security-only support) |
| `frontend` job | 72 s | Pass |
| `ziggy` job | 7 s | Pass: the committed route list matches |
| Regen gate | 15 s | Fails with 3 paths of new drift; the GitLab job blocks on new drift. Below |
| Accessibility gate | 65 s | **0 violations** in 16 page checks; 26 to 29 rules passed on each page |
| A second `bin\weld.ps1 up` | 188 s | **Emptied the local database.** Fixed the same night, below |

From an empty folder to a signed-in WayneUI dashboard took about four and a half minutes of machine time once the blank page was fixed, and to every gate green about eight. Your network and disk will move both numbers; the shape will not change much, because the first `up` is mostly Composer and npm downloading.

The `create-project` path:

| Step | Time | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `composer create-project waynestate/weld` | 156 s | Installed **0.1.2**, the newest tag (2026-11-03): 67 commits behind `main`, from before WayneUI drew the app |
| `npm ci` | 14 s | Pass |
| `bin\weld.ps1 up` | 159 s | Up; the same blank page |
| `bin\weld.ps1 test` |  | **Fails.** PROCTOR's `composer-audit` check found 7 advisories in Symfony components locked in 0.1.2, published after the tag, and one trusted-proxy test failed. `main` passes both |

That is PROCTOR doing its job on a three-day-old lock: the gate caught advisories nobody had to go looking for. It is also a reason not to start from 0.1.2; 0.1.3, tagged later the same day, carries the patched lock and WayneUI.

### WayneUI in the pages[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#wayneui-in-the-pages)

After the fix, every page of the new app was WayneUI's: the app bar with the shield and the theme switch, the sidebar that turns into a drawer on a phone, breadcrumbs, cards, the form fields and the footer, in light and dark. Tab moved through the bar with a visible gold focus ring. The axe gate, run with reduced motion on, found nothing to report on any page, at either width, in either scheme.

### A port: one small app onto WELD[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#a-port-one-small-app-onto-weld)

The second workload asked a plainer question: how much of a real app's work is left once WELD has done its part? The app was the smallest useful one in the stack's proof corpus: a read-only JSON feed, about 100 lines of raw PHP with no framework, one Oracle query and two optional filters, with its own error shape for bad input.

On the fresh clone it became:

- a controller that keeps the old contract exactly: the same query string, the same validation and the same `{"message", "error": true}` body with a 400 for bad input, the same row keys, and nulls turned into empty strings as the old feed did;
- a `ProgramSource` interface with a fake source of made-up rows for local work and tests, and an Oracle source that runs the old query, kept outside the repository, on WELD's `oracle` connection;
- a new page drawn by WayneUI that reads the same JSON: a filter card with a native select and a text field, and WayneUI's sortable data table with a caption;
- nine Pest tests for the contract.

| What | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Size | 369 lines added across 16 files, including the tests and the regenerated route list |
| Time | 11 minutes 20 seconds of wall clock for the agent that wrote it, from first file to last check; a person new to Laravel will take longer |
| `composer ci` | Pass first time apart from formatting: Pint fixed 2 style issues, Prettier 1 file. PHPStan level 8 passed the new code as written |
| `composer proctor` | Pass, the same single warning |
| `frontend` job | Pass after Prettier |
| Accessibility gate on the new page | 0 violations at both widths and both schemes; 31 to 32 rules passed |

What WELD supplied without a line of the port's own: sign-in in front of the page, HELMET's security headers on every response (the JSON included), the database connection for the real query, WayneUI for every pixel, and the gates that judged the result.

Two honest differences from the old app. A POST now gets Laravel's own 405 body instead of the old JSON one. And the Oracle source was never run: the proof never connects to Oracle or Banner, so the real query is only shown to be wired, not to work.

### What it caught in WELD[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-it-caught-in-weld)

A run that only finds praise was not looking hard enough. This one found these, and every finding is about WELD, not the ported app:

- **Fixed: a blank page on the first open.** The Vite container ran `vite --host`, so Laravel's Vite plugin wrote the address it listened on, `http://[::]:5173`, into `public/hot`, and every page asked the browser to load its scripts from an address it cannot reach. `compose.yaml` now sets `LARAVEL_SAIL=1` instead, which makes the plugin listen on all addresses in the container and hand the browser `http://localhost:5173`. Checked by `tests/Unit/LocalStackTest.php` and by the pages rendering on the next run.
- **Fixed: every second `up` on Windows emptied the local database.** `bin\weld.ps1 up` created the SQLite file with `New-Item -Force`, which truncates a file that already exists. One signed-in user before the second `up`, none after. It now creates the file only when it is missing (macOS and Linux used `touch` and were never affected). Checked by the same test and by a later `up` with the fix, which kept the user.
- **Fixed: `create-project` installed 0.1.2.** The newest tag was from before WayneUI drew the app, and its locked Symfony components now carry advisories. 0.1.3 (2026-11-06) is the fix, and the pipeline it was tagged from was green.
- **Open: a new page on Windows says "Page not found".** Docker Desktop passes edits to existing files into the Vite container, but not new files, so Inertia cannot find a page added after `up` until Vite restarts: `docker compose restart vite`. Polling would see new files, but it took 21 seconds to notice a save and kept the Vite container at about a third of one CPU, so it is not the default. See [Troubleshooting](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html).
- **Open: the regen gate.** Run by hand, today's Sourdough stops before generating, at its check for read access to Playbook, a private package; in CI that check is skipped and the app is generated with Playbook wired, which WELD does not require. With CI set, the gate reported 3 paths of new drift on top of the recorded baseline. Fixed the same day: WELD took Sourdough's `SkipEnvFile` and `TestCase`, Sourdough took WELD's `DummyAppKey`, and the gate reports no new drift. Sourdough's Inertia template still draws with Tailwind while WELD draws with WayneUI, so the front-end files stay in the baseline until that template moves to WayneUI.
- **Open: a warm `up` still reinstalls.** The second `up` took 188 seconds because it runs `composer install`, ADVISOR's install and a full `npm ci` again. It is correct, just slow; a faster path for an app that is already up is worth having.
- **Open, small: Sign in lands on the welcome page.** SESAME signs the user in and returns them to `/`, where the button now reads Open the dashboard. One more click than it needs.

### What this does not prove[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-this-does-not-prove)

- Only Windows ran. `bin/weld.sh` on macOS and Linux was not exercised, apart from reading that it creates the SQLite file with `touch`.
- Nothing was deployed. Citadel, Squire's release script and the container contract are proven elsewhere, not here.
- SESAME ran its fake driver only; CAS and Entra ID were not part of this run.
- No real data, Oracle or Banner. The port's real query was never executed.
- One port of one small app is a sample of one. A larger app, with forms that write, would take longer and find more.
- The timings are from one machine on one night. Treat them as the shape, not a promise.

### Run it yourself[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#run-it-yourself)

The same bend test on your machine, from an empty folder:

Windows

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/weld.git my-app
cd my-app
.\bin\weld.ps1 up
.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
.\bin\weld.ps1 test
docker compose run --rm app composer proctor
```

macOS / Linux

```sh
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/weld.git my-app
cd my-app
bin/weld.sh up
bin/weld.sh doctor
bin/weld.sh test
docker compose run --rm app composer proctor
```

Then open [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000), sign in, and run `bin\weld.ps1 up` (or `bin/weld.sh up`) a second time: your data should still be there.

## Status[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/status.html#status)

This page records what is on the bench today: the state of every part welded into WELD, plus the gaps still open for the backlog.

HELMET, SESAME and PROCTOR are welded in from Packagist; the rest of the cast is on Packagist too and gets welded on in turn. For what each part does in WELD, see [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html).

### What is on the bench today[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/status.html#what-is-on-the-bench-today)

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `composer.json` | `waynestate/weld`, requires PHP `^8.3`, and the lock file resolves for 8.3.0 |
| `.env.example` | sets `APP_NAME=WELD`, `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr` and `SESSION_DRIVER=database` |
| Index length | `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` keeps index keys under Citadel's MySQL 5.6 767-byte cap |
| `.gitattributes` | sets `* text=auto eol=lf` |
| CI contract | `composer ci` runs validate, tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready check and audit, the same command on GitLab and GitHub |
| Pinstripe presets | `pint.json` and `phpstan.neon` still copy Pinstripe's 0.1 Laravel presets; Pinstripe 0.1.4 is on Packagist (tagged), and they switch to `includes: vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/...` when WELD requires it |
| HELMET | runs its security headers and CSP middleware in the global chain, so every response carries the baseline; the Vite build takes the per-request nonce; trusted proxies are a literal list in `bootstrap/app.php`; `/up` stays Laravel's built-in health route |
| SESAME | owns sign-in at `/login` and `/logout`; the fake driver stands in for the identity provider locally, and CAS is an env change away |
| PROCTOR | measures WELD against CREED's `policy.json` as a CI job (`composer proctor`): warnings pass, failures block |
| Password auth | the starter kit's password auth (register, login, password reset, two-factor) is removed on purpose; the door is SESAME's |
| License | MIT |

### Gaps for the backlog[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/status.html#gaps-for-the-backlog)

The Laravel base has landed; the gaps below are the stack packages and the deploy path that have not.

- The stack packages are dependencies now: SESAME and HELMET in `require`, CREED and PROCTOR in `require-dev`, all from Packagist. The items that waited on them (SESAME W1, HELMET W17 and W28, PROCTOR's `Checked` targets, CREED W25) can be checked against the installed packages. Preflight portability (W8, W10, W12, W13, W16, W24), Pinstripe (W2, W32) and WayneUI (W2) are not wired into WELD yet.
- The Squire kit in `deploy/` now carries the Citadel deploy path: a Dockerfile mirroring the platform image, an entrypoint and an idempotent release script, so W10, W12, W16 and W24 hold for that path. Still plans: worker and scheduler process types (W8), the non-root, group-0, 8080 contract (W13), the restart commands in the release script (W22), and the deploy-time queue/scheduler work (W19, W21, W23).
- The JS side of the coding standard (W32) is configured but not in CI.
- Unverified: OpenShift arbitrary-UID text on a primary Red Hat page; `serversideup/php` behavior under a random UID; Pest 4's PHP floor; `spatie/laravel-health` scheduler and queue checks; whether Laravel's health route runs before `TrustHosts`; whether the old CSRF middleware name is still an alias.
- Decision needed: queue mode on Citadel (W19). The scheduled-worker pattern is a stopgap. Confirm with the deploy kit project whether Citadel can run a cron-driven `schedule:run` at all.
- Decision needed: `spatie/laravel-health` or our own `/ready` (W11, W23).
- Decision needed: whether WELD keeps Fortify for a non-SSO mode.
- Decision needed: SSR on by default or off.

## Which command when[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/which-command.html#which-command-when)

This page is the canonical copy of the "which command when" table. Every README of a stack project that ships one of these commands carries the same table, word for word; change it here first, then copy it into those READMEs (WELD, Squire, PROCTOR, Sourdough, Booster and Rollcall).

Several stack commands sound alike (`weld:doctor`, `squire doctor`, `proctor check`) and do different jobs. Find your question in the second column and run the command beside it. The doctors look at setup, the proctor grades against policy, and the gate decides deploys: same waiting room, different appointments.

| Command | What it checks | When to run it | Where it runs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composer ci` | **Will my pipeline pass?** The repo's own CI contract, the same command the pipeline runs: validation, the tests, Pint, PHPStan, `composer audit` and whatever checks the repo adds. | Before every push. | App repo, CI |
| `bin/weld.sh doctor` or `.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor` (both run `php artisan weld:doctor`) | **Does my WELD app hold together?** The app key, writable `storage` and `bootstrap/cache`, the database connection and pending migrations. One PASS, WARN or FAIL line each; exit 1 on a FAIL. Standards are PROCTOR's. | After `up`, when the app will not start, and after every deploy off Citadel. | App repo (in the app container), deploy host (in the app container) |
| `vendor/bin/squire doctor` | **Is my Citadel release setup right?** `build.sh`, the release scripts, the health check, script hygiene, line endings, secrets kept out of git and the local parity setup, against Squire's rules. Exit 1 on a failed rule. The lock file, audit and MySQL 5.6 checks are handed to PROCTOR. | After `squire init` or `squire update`, and before the first deploy. | App repo, CI |
| `vendor/bin/squire init --check` | **Have the files Squire wrote drifted from its templates?** Missing, outdated or edited copies. Writes nothing; exit 1 on drift. | After you upgrade Squire (then run `squire update`), and in CI. | App repo, CI |
| `vendor/bin/squire doctor oracle`, or `php artisan oracle:check` in WELD and Sourdough's Laravel apps | **Can my app reach Oracle?** The `ORACLE_*` settings, the host, the port, the `oci8` driver and the login, in plain language, printing setting names and never values. Silent when the app has no Oracle settings. | After you fill in the `ORACLE_*` settings, or when a connection fails. Squire's `release.sh` runs the same check on every release, as a report. | App repo, deploy host |
| `vendor/bin/proctor check` (`composer proctor` in WELD and Sourdough's apps) | **Does my app meet CREED's policy?** The PHP floor, Laravel, Node and MySQL end of life, the committed lock, `composer audit`, open-ended constraints, portability, MySQL 5.6 safety, overrides and the rest of its checks. Exit 1 on a FAIL. | Before you merge; the pipeline runs it too. | App repo, CI |
| `vendor/bin/proctor gate` | **May this commit deploy?** The deploy-time subset of `proctor check`, ratcheted against the last release's verdict, so a deploy that makes nothing worse goes. Exit 1 is a no-go. | At deploy time. Squire's `release.sh` calls it for you. | Deploy host |
| `sourdough manifest --check` | **Which managed files did I change since Sourdough baked my app?** Managed files that changed or are missing against `.sourdough/manifest.json`; seeded files are yours and never reported. Exit 1 on a change. | Before `sourdough feed`. | App repo, CI |
| `sourdough feed --dry-run` | **Is my app behind its Sourdough template?** The plan a feed would apply, with nothing written. Exit 1 when feeding would change files. | After you install a new Sourdough, and in CI to catch an app falling behind. | App repo, CI |
| `booster plan` | **What does my upgrade take?** The ordered PHP, Laravel and front-end hops, the dependencies that block them, and advisory PHPCompatibility and PHPStan scans. Changes nothing. | Before an upgrade, and when PROCTOR says your PHP or Laravel is past support. | App repo |
| `booster replay check` | **Does my app still answer the same after a change?** Replays the requests in `booster-replay.json` and compares the answers with the ones `booster replay record` saved. Exit 1 on a changed answer. | After an upgrade hop or a hand fix, once you have a recording. | App repo (in Docker) |
| `booster init --check` | **Are Booster's coding-tab playbooks current?** The playbooks in `.agents/skills`. Changes nothing; exit 1 when one is missing or out of date. | After you upgrade Booster, and in CI. | App repo, CI |
| `php bin/regen-check.php --generated <dir>` | **Is WELD still Sourdough's Inertia shape?** WELD, file by file, against a fresh `sourdough new --inertia`; fails only on drift that `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` does not already accept. | When Sourdough's Inertia shape or WELD changes. | WELD repo, CI |
| `rollcall report` | **Where does the whole fleet stand?** The latest scan's totals against CREED's policy: PHP, Laravel, the auth package, PROCTOR results and the end-of-life burn-down. Always exit 0; it never gates. | After `rollcall scan`, on the scan's schedule. | CI (a scheduled scan job) |

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/which-command.html#related)

- [Commands](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html)
- [Oracle](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html)
